channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: KEPCO Breach Exposes 1.5 Million Customer Records
item.description: A threat actor breached KEPCO’s internal network, accessing two systems that stored customer, employee, and contractor data. The intrusion leveraged an undisclosed vulnerability in the company’s network perimeter, enabling unauthorized data exfiltration and potential credential compromise. KEPCO has issued a security advisory and is conducting a forensic investigation, urging affected users to monitor accounts and change passwords.

item.title: Chrome Extended Stable Channel Updated to 156.0.8078.114
item.description: Google Chrome’s Extended Stable channel updated to 156.0.8078.114 for Windows and macOS, extending the stable release schedule. The update lists changes, with security fixes pending a later release, and will roll out over the next days or weeks. Users may review the change log, file bugs, or use the community forum while awaiting the security patch.

item.title: CVE-2026-134056 - Out-of-bounds write in padded block cipher decryption in AWS-LC
item.description: Bulletin ID: 2026-196-AWS Publication Date: 11/23/2026 12:00 PM PST Description: We identified CVE-2026-134056, an out-of-bounds write issue in AWS-LC's padded block cipher decryption. If the output buffer is the minimum documented size, AWS-LC can write one byte past its end. The aws-lc-rs StreamingDecryptingKey API has a similar issue with cbc_pkcs7 and ecb_pkcs7.

item.title: Trump Names Industry Veteran Davies as Acting Cyber Director
item.description: Trump appointed Kirsten Davies as National Cyber Director, signaling a shift toward industry expertise amid outages and geopolitical tensions. The move follows criticism of cyber leadership and aims to leverage Davies' private sector experience to strengthen U.S. cyber defenses. The appointment is expected to influence policy direction and coordination with industry partners, though no immediate operational changes have been announced.

item.title: OpenRouter Removes AI Providers for Data Handling Violations
item.description: OpenRouter removed three AI providers after discovering they violated data-handling policies and exposed sensitive user prompts and secrets. The policy breach leaked proprietary prompts, potentially compromising client confidentiality and violating OpenRouter's privacy commitments. OpenRouter suspended the providers, issued a public notice, and is reviewing vetting procedures to prevent future violations.

item.title: Chrome iOS Stable 158 Released with Stability Improvements
item.description: Google released Chrome Stable 158 (158.0.8127.86) for iOS, adding stability and performance improvements to the mobile browser. The update addresses minor bugs and optimizes rendering, reducing memory usage and enhancing page load times on iOS devices. The new build will be available on the App Store within hours, and users are encouraged to update to benefit from the fixes.

item.title: LaLiga Data Breach Exposes Fans Personal Information
item.description: LaLiga disclosed a breach that exposed personal data of its users and some affiliated clubs. The theft included names, email addresses, phone numbers, and other sensitive information, raising significant privacy and regulatory concerns. LaLiga notified affected users, launched incident response, and is cooperating with law enforcement to trace the attack.

item.title: MISP Advises Hotfix for Pre-v2.5.53 Vulnerabilities
item.description: The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security issued advisory AV26-1197, noting that MISP versions prior to 2.5.53 contain multiple security vulnerabilities. A quick hotfix, version 2.5.53, addresses the identified flaws, and administrators are urged to review the provided links and apply updates as soon as possible. Failure to patch may leave MISP installations vulnerable to exploitation of the disclosed weaknesses.

item.title: AI Detects New Attacks by Learning Normal Behavior
item.description: Arctic Wolf's AI threat detection platform identifies new attacks by learning normal user, device, and system behavior. The system flags deviations that may indicate emerging threats, enabling security teams to investigate and respond to previously unseen attacks. This approach expands detection coverage beyond signature-based methods, improving overall security posture for organizations worldwide.

item.title: New Framework Traces Decade of Ransomware Actors
item.description: A new attribution framework enables security teams to trace ransomware actors across a decade of operations. The framework aggregates metadata from ransomware campaigns, correlating signatures and infrastructure to identify individual threat actors, thereby improving threat intelligence and response. Security teams can adopt the framework to enhance attribution accuracy, integrate with existing SIEMs, and prioritize defensive measures against identified actors.

item.title: Webworm Modifies SoftEther VPN to Evade Detection
item.description: The China-aligned threat actor Webworm is suspected of deploying a custom SoftEther VPN Bridge variant designed to conceal itself from security tools. The modified bridge removes recognizable detection fingerprints and masquerades as network-monitoring software, enabling covert remote access to compromised networks. Defenders should monitor anomalous VPN traffic, verify SoftEther installations against known hashes, and apply patches to mitigate potential exploitation.

item.title: USN-9187-1: libssh vulnerabilities
item.description: This issue only affected Ubuntu 16.04 LTS, Ubuntu 18.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-59843) Mikhail Ilin and Saransh Rana discovered that libssh did not correctly sanitize shell metacharacters when expanding usernames in ProxyCommand strings. An attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain sensitive information. (CVE-2026-59846) Ben Smyth discovered that libssh incorrectly verified AES-GCM authentication tags when built with the OpenSSL backend.

item.title: CrowdStrike Acquires Zscaler for $43.9B
item.description: CrowdStrike announced the acquisition of Zscaler in a $43.9 billion deal, aiming to expand its AI-driven security portfolio. The purchase reflects CEO George Kurtz’s vision of building the largest AI safety and security company worldwide. The transaction is expected to integrate Zscaler’s cloud security platform with CrowdStrike’s endpoint protection, pending regulatory approval.

item.title: GlobeTopper Suffers Cyberattack Causing Financial and Operational Losses
item.description: B2B top-up solutions provider GlobeTopper suffered a cyberattack that disrupted its business operations and compromised digital assets. Attackers redeemed digital gift cards valued at $70,000, resulting in an estimated total operational revenue loss of $2.5 million for the company. Organizations should review digital asset transaction controls and implement strict access monitoring on top-up management systems.

item.title: China-Nexus Actor Exploits Medical Imaging Zero-Day via Cairn
item.description: A China-nexus threat actor targeted East Asian universities by deploying the Cairn penetration testing tool to execute attacks. The adversary exploited an unpatched zero-day vulnerability in a medical imaging application, escalating privileges from flaw discovery to root access within 11 minutes. Security teams must monitor for unauthorized Cairn execution and audit medical imaging software for unauthenticated access vectors.

item.title: Red Hat Issues freerdp Patch for RHEL 9
item.description: Red Hat released an important freerdp update for RHEL 9, addressing several security vulnerabilities. The flaws could allow attackers to execute arbitrary code or exfiltrate session data, yet no active exploitation has been reported. Security teams should apply the freerdp patch immediately, verify remote desktop configurations, and monitor for suspicious activity.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Important Netpbm Patch for RHEL 10
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the netpbm package affecting Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10 installations. The underlying security flaws received an Important severity rating from Red Hat Product Security, with detailed base scores published in accompanying advisories. System administrators should apply the updated netpbm packages via standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux package management systems.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Netpbm Update for RHEL 9.8 EUS
item.description: Red Hat issued a security update addressing vulnerabilities in the netpbm package for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8 Extended Update Support. Red Hat Product Security categorized the security impact as Important, providing Common Vulnerability Scoring System base scores across referenced advisories. Administrators managing Extended Update Support environments must deploy the updated netpbm packages to mitigate potential security risks.

item.title: Splunk Advisory Affects Multiple Products, Requires Upgrade
item.description: Splunk issued a security advisory (AV26-1196) affecting multiple products, including Enterprise, Enterprise Security, PCI Compliance, and SOAR, with versions prior to specified releases. The vulnerabilities could enable unauthorized access or privilege escalation within Splunk deployments, but no active exploitation has been confirmed. Administrators should review the provided links, upgrade to newer versions, and enforce access controls to mitigate risk.

item.title: Microsoft Patches Exploited Azure API Management Flaw Targeting Energy Sector Credentials
item.description: Microsoft patched an Azure API Management flaw that attackers exploited to target Norwegian energy companies and other sectors. The vulnerability let attackers read protected configuration data and credential vaults, potentially exposing API secrets and sensitive information. Microsoft urged affected customers to apply the update or configuration changes immediately to block unauthorized credential access.

item.title: Hackers Exploit Microsoft Cloud Flaw Against Norwegian Energy Firms
item.description: Hackers exploited a Microsoft cloud security vulnerability to target sensitive credentials at Equinor and Skagerak Energi. The flaw permitted unauthorized access to configuration secrets, potentially exposing login information, though no confirmed data loss was reported. Microsoft issued a patch and urged affected customers to update their Azure services to close the vulnerability.

item.title: Spring AI Vulnerability Affects Multiple Versions
item.description: Spring AI versions prior to 1.0.11, 1.1.10, 2.0.2.1, and 2.0.3 suffer a broken logical grouping expression flaw in TypesenseFilterExpressionConverter. The flaw can cause improper query parsing, potentially exposing data or causing denial of service. Upgrade to the latest Spring AI release or apply the vendor patch to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Meta Muse AI Hallucinates, Shares External App Data
item.description: Meta’s Muse AI agent reportedly accessed data from other applications and produced hallucinated responses during user interactions. The incident highlights limitations in the model’s knowledge boundaries and the risk of unintended data leakage. Meta should refine data access controls and improve hallucination mitigation to safeguard user privacy and information integrity.

item.title: Apache Solr Health-Check Vulnerability Disclosed
item.description: Apache Solr versions prior to 10.1.0 and 9.11.0 contain a health-check flaw that can trigger unintended functionality, referenced by CVE-2026-86312. The flaw allows attackers to invoke the ping endpoint, potentially causing unauthorized actions or information disclosure within the Solr instance. Administrators should upgrade to Solr 10.1.0 or later, or apply the vendor-issued patch, and verify that health-check endpoints are secured.

item.title: RHEL9 Podman Update Fixes Important Security Flaw
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the podman container engine on RHEL9 to address a critical flaw. The patch fixes an undisclosed vulnerability rated Important by Red Hat Product Security, with CVSS scores linked through CVE references. Administrators should apply the podman update immediately to prevent exploitation and maintain secure container orchestration environments.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102507: Important: webkit2gtk3 security update
item.description: An update for webkit2gtk3 is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.4 Update Services for SAP Solutions. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Grafana Update Addresses Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities
item.description: A Grafana security update for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10 addresses multiple vulnerabilities that could enable remote code execution through the web interface. The vulnerabilities are rated Important, with CVSS base scores listed in the CVE references, indicating high severity potential for exploitation. Red Hat has released the update; administrators should apply the patch immediately to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Synology DSM Vulnerability Affects Versions Before 7.4.1
item.description: DiskStation Manager (DSM) versions prior to 7.4.1 contain a vulnerability that could allow unauthorized access or privilege escalation. The flaw permits attackers to exploit a logic error in DSM’s authentication flow, potentially bypassing user credentials and gaining elevated privileges. Administrators should upgrade to the latest DSM release or apply the vendor-issued patch, and enforce strict access controls to mitigate exploitation.

item.title: RHSA-2026:100561: Important: OpenJDK 11.0.33.1 ELS Security Update For Portable Linux Builds
item.description: An update is now available for OpenJDK. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: FBI NCIC Database Targeted in Second Cyber Incident
item.description: The FBI’s National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database was targeted in a second cyber incident reported this month. The attack compromised access to records on fugitives, warrants, criminal histories, and missing persons, potentially exposing sensitive law-enforcement data. Investigators are assessing the breach scope, and security teams should monitor for unauthorized access attempts to similar databases.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102405: Important: qt5-qtdeclarative security update
item.description: An update for qt5-qtdeclarative is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.6 Extended Update Support. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Trump Names Davies National Cyber Czar
item.description: President Trump has confirmed appointing Pentagon CIO John Davies as national cyber director after widespread support. Davies, who has served as acting director, will lead DoD cyber strategy and coordinate federal cyber defense efforts. The appointment aims to strengthen overall U.S. cyber posture, contingent on interagency cooperation and resource allocation.

item.title: JetBrains Advises Updates for Multiple Product Vulnerabilities
item.description: JetBrains announced vulnerabilities affecting Junie, Junie CLI, and Junie GitHub Action, with affected versions listed in advisory AV26-1192. The flaws stem from insufficient input validation and insecure configuration defaults, enabling unauthorized code execution or privilege escalation, though no active exploitation has been reported. JetBrains recommends applying the latest patches for all affected versions and reviewing configuration settings to mitigate risk.

item.title: Multiple High-Impact Vulnerabilities Exploit Remote Code Paths
item.description: This week’s recap highlights several high-impact vulnerabilities, including a VMware 0-Day, Java4Shell, NGINX2Root, and Ruby2Shell, that exploit remote code execution paths. The flaws enable attackers to pivot from one compromised system to another, expanding lateral movement. Vendors have released patches; security teams should apply them promptly and monitor for exploitation attempts.

item.title: N-Able Releases Patch for Critical CVE-2026-134624
item.description: N-Able disclosed a critical flaw, CVE-2026-134624, that was exploited during a Mail Assure cyberattack targeting its services. The vulnerability allowed attackers to gain unauthorized access to administrative functions, potentially enabling data exfiltration or service disruption. N-Able released a patch and advised customers to apply the update immediately to mitigate the risk.

item.title: GL.iNet Cloud Compromise Deploys Malware to Routers and KVMs
item.description: Attackers compromised GL.iNet’s GoodCloud remote-management service and used it to install malware on connected routers and KVM devices. The breach exploited unauthorized cloud access, enabling remote code execution on device firmware and allowing persistent control and data exfiltration. GL.iNet has not yet released a patch; teams should isolate affected devices, update firmware when available, and monitor for anomalous traffic.

item.title: AI Agent Identity Gaps Span Multiple Platforms
item.description: AI agents operating across multiple platforms create security gaps when no single vendor can observe or control their actions, according to Token Security. The shared responsibility problem complicates agent identity, permission, and accountability management for organizations. Organizations should assign clear ownership and accountability for agent identities and permissions across platforms.

item.title: Huntress Begins EU Data Hosting in Frankfurt
item.description: Huntress has started European Union data hosting, with Phase 1 storing certain data in Frankfurt. The company said other data currently remains in the United States while Phase 2 is planned. Customers should review the available regional data residency details to fully understand which information is hosted in each location.

item.title: N-Able MailAssure Vulnerability Advisory
item.description: N-Able issued advisory AV26-1191 for MailAssure before 20261121.1943, noting a vulnerability. The flaw may allow unauthorized access to email data or compromise the integrity of mail transmissions, though no exploitation reports have been confirmed. Administrators are advised to review the provided links, apply available updates, and monitor for any anomalous activity.

item.title: NVIDIA Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
item.description: NVIDIA reinstated Jensen Huang as president, chief executive officer, and board director on November 23, 2026, after a unanimous board vote. The decision took effect immediately, but an independent board inquiry into reports that a foreign intelligence effort targeted Huang remains open. NVIDIA said the board met with Huang several times and received additional information.

item.title: Wiz Research Reports Agentic Framework Cloud Intrusions
item.description: Agentic offensive frameworks such as ARTEX are driving a surge in cloud intrusions, as reported by Wiz Research. These frameworks enable automated, high-velocity attacks that exploit misconfigurations and weak IAM controls, causing unauthorized data exfiltration and service disruption across cloud environments. Security teams should monitor for ARTEX-related activity, enforce least-privilege IAM, and deploy detection rules to spot noisy, machine-speed attacks.

item.title: Red Hat Advises Updates for Multiple RHEL Versions
item.description: Red Hat issued advisory AV26-1190 affecting all RHEL 6-10, Hardened Images, and OpenShift 4-5. The advisory references multiple undisclosed vulnerabilities across these products, with no CVE IDs provided, implying potential remote code execution or privilege escalation risks. Administrators should review Red Hat’s links and apply available patches as soon as they are released.

item.title: EU Academy Access Disabled After Data Exposure Attack
item.description: The European Commission disabled public access to the EU Academy platform after a cyberattack exposed users’ personal data. The breach involved unauthorized access to the learning platform’s database, potentially compromising contact information and enrollment records. The Commission has not disclosed the number of affected users; security teams should monitor for credential misuse and enforce stricter access controls.

item.title: Fake Claude AI App Distributes RevStealer Infostealer
item.description: Hackers distributed RevStealer, a Windows infostealer, via a counterfeit Claude AI desktop application promising free access. The 101 MB archive launches malware that harvests saved passwords, browser sessions, and cryptocurrency wallet data without opening a chat window. Security teams should verify application authenticity, block the download source, and deploy endpoint protection to detect and remove RevStealer.

item.title: Vmcloudoor Backdoor Targets Alibaba, Tencent, Huawei Clouds
item.description: The newly discovered Linux backdoor, Vmcloudoor, covertly commandeers cloud servers, enabling attackers to exfiltrate sensitive files. Designed to infect virtual machines on Chinese cloud platforms, it masquerades as a legitimate cloud-management agent, reducing detection by administrators. Security teams should isolate affected instances, update to the latest vendor patches, and monitor for unauthorized agent activity.

item.title: Cloudflare Builds DNS Testing Tools for Internal Framework
item.description: Cloudflare developed internal tools to extend its testing framework for networking protocols, focusing on DNS. The new DNS tooling enables teams to probe protocol behavior, identify edge cases, and validate performance under load. These tools are available internally and can be leveraged by security teams to assess DNS resilience and detect anomalies.

item.title: USN-9186-1: Tomcat vulnerabilities
item.description: Tomcat 10 has been updated to 10.1.61 in Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS and Ubuntu 26.10. Tomcat 11 has been updated to 11.0.27 in Ubuntu 26.04 LTS and Ubuntu 26.10. In addition to security fixes, the updated packages contain bug fixes, new features, and possibly incompatible changes.

item.title: WordPress Site Hosts 13 ClickFix Malware Traps
item.description: A compromised WordPress site hosted 13 ClickFix traps from three malware kits, each presenting a fake security check. The traps use social engineering to convince users to paste malicious commands, a phishing kit requiring user interaction. Security teams should remove infected plugins, update WordPress core, and monitor for similar deceptive traps.

item.title: PHP Session Overwrite Flaw Enables Remote Code Execution
item.description: A PHP session overwrite flaw lets attackers inject malicious data during an interrupted overwrite, triggering deserialization and remote code execution on apps. The flaw, part of the PHP2Shell chain, exploits improper session data handling and can be triggered without authentication, risking server compromise. No patch exists yet; admins should disable session overwrite or apply custom fixes to block deserialization attacks.

item.title: IBM Issues Advisory for Multiple Vulnerabilities
item.description: IBM disclosed vulnerabilities in Engineering AI Hub up to 1.4.0 and Guardium Data Protection up to 12.2, enabling unauthorized access. Flaws stem from insufficient input validation and privilege checks, with CVSS 7.0-8.5, though no exploitation reported. Apply the latest firmware updates and review advisory links for mitigation guidance to secure deployments.
